response.text:
Sampled HR@10 with 99 negatives is a protocol-specific objective: it can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog ranking, even in expectation. Keep the pinned macro validation HR@10 as the selection criterion; use full-catalog probes as complementary stress measurements. [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establishes this inconsistency. [Prakash et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) also finds negative-sampling choices interact with dataset popularity distributions, with aggregate performance masking head/mid/tail differences. Report per-category and popularity/history-length strata, defining popularity from training histories only.

Embedding geometry offers hypotheses, not a validated substitute for HR@10. [Guo et al. (ICML 2024)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html) links embedding collapse to limited recommendation-model scalability; it does not establish effective rank as a universal predictor of this SASRec benchmark. Practical implication: exclude padding, state whether spectra use singular values or squared singular values, and measure embedding norms alongside effective rank. Raw training margins are score-scale-sensitive: positive score rescaling increases margins while preserving rankings. Compare rank-based separation and verify whether probe changes consistently track validation gains across trials.

Recommended uncertainty analysis: paired user bootstrap within each category, recomputing the equally weighted four-category mean and model difference. This estimates user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and training seed; it does not capture candidate-sampling variability, training randomness, or repeated-search selection bias. User-level uncertainty is emphasized by the [2024 Dagstuhl evaluation report](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/04dagstuhl-reports/volume14/issue05/DagRep.14.5/DagRep.14.5.pdf). Twenty users’ unseen-item lists support descriptive coverage, concentration and stability checks, not relevance estimates without held-out labels. Ratings, review sentiment and simulator diversity/conformity remain unmeasured.
